name: equal_effort
description: PLACEHOLDER -- NOT RUNNABLE AS SHIPPED. Isolates evaluation quality from search volume by giving DeepSetsBotExp whatever extra wall clock it needs to evaluate the SAME number of positions per turn as the stock-speed baseline, instead of the same wall clock. The answer to 'is the network better, or is the heuristic agent just searching more?' is this matchup's win rate. Fill in the two TBDs from a calibration run before submitting anything.
_how_to_fill_this_in: Runs the calibration block below (20 games, DeepSetsBotExp vs SakkirinaScaled, both at
stock speed) and prints mean evaluations per turn for each agent plus a SUGGESTED
2. Put that number into matchups[0].env.SOT_TIME_SCALE below, and set matchups[0].timeout to
ceil(9.8 * that scale) + 2 -- the engine clock has to be able to accommodate the bot's own
enlarged per-turn cap, or every turn ends as a TURN_TIMEOUT.
3. Re-run --calibrate with those values to CONFIRM the two evals/turn figures actually meet.
Evaluations per turn is only approximately linear in the time budget (tree reuse and the
rule-based fast paths do not scale with the clock), so the first suggestion is a starting
point, not an answer. Iterate until the two agents are within a few percent.
The harness REFUSES to run any matchup whose timeout or env still says TBD -- a run that
quietly fell back to SOT_TIME_SCALE=1.0 would produce a full set of numbers labelled
'equal effort' that measured nothing of the kind.

matchups.label: equal_effort
matchups.note: The baseline stays at 1.0 (stock SakkirinaSolo timing) on purpose -- it is the fixed point the treatment is matched TO. Only DeepSetsBotExp's clock moves.

matchups.label: calibrate_stock_speed
matchups.note: SakkirinaScaled rather than SakkirinaSolo because stock SakkirinaSolo emits no throughput telemetry at all, and at SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE=1.0 the two are timing-identical. This is how the stock baseline's evaluations per turn gets measured.
